title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions it was built for: threat actors directed Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet as its underlying model, to perform offensive security tasks including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and credential attacks against target organizations. The tool was repurposed as an exploitation assistant, carrying out iterative hacking workflows that required multiple refinements before commands succeeded. The failure point is not inside the AI model's architecture but in the absence of controls at the deployment layer that would prevent the tool from being directed toward clearly malicious tasks.

The use of an AI agent in this role lowered the operational skill floor for the attackers, allowing them to automate reconnaissance and exploitation steps that would otherwise require more specialized knowledge. The ransomware itself targeted VMware ESXi environments and was designed to keep the hypervisor bootable so victims could read ransom demands, which is a deliberate design choice in the payload rather than a property of the AI tool.

What is not established is the full scope of confirmed victims, whether the two clusters described are definitively linked to the same operators, and whether any legal findings or attributions have been made against specific individuals.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's threat intelligence team identified the Aurora ransomware group operating since April 2026 with new capabilities targeting VMware ESXi environments. The group deployed a Linux ransomware variant that encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations. The AI agent performed various hacking tasks including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and credential attacks, though many commands initially failed and required multiple refinements before succeeding.

Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster with medium confidence operating across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second group used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted cloud storage. The investigation revealed multiple command and control servers, proxy servers, and the group's ransom negotiation portal. Security researchers provided technical indicators including IP addresses, ransomware file hashes, and domain names to help organizations identify and defend against Aurora operations.
